references.phrase: closed subset of a topological space
references.context: General topology: closed F⊆X exactly when X\F is open in the specified topology; this depends on the ambient X and is distinct from Zariski-closed subschemes.
references.reason: Closed-set status is a reusable topological prerequisite independently of irreducibility.
references.matching_note: Match contextually to closure formulation's topologically closed subset.

references.phrase: union of two proper closed subsets
references.disposition: The prohibition of writing X=F∪G with F,G proper closed is the defining predicate of irreducibility. Union is an ordinary underlying set operation, not a separately required special 'union of proper closed sets' concept.
An empty space is explicitly excluded from irreducibility in this formulation even though alternative conventions may exist.

references.phrase: cannot be written as union of two proper closed subsets
references.disposition: The definition rules out any such pair, not merely disjoint closed decompositions.
